name: FIX (Features Interpretable to eXperts)
description: Feature-based methods are commonly used to explain model predictions, but these methods often implicitly assume that interpretable features are readily available. However, this is often not the case for high-dimensional data, and it can be hard even for domain experts to mathematically specify which features are important. Can we instead automatically extract collections or groups of features that are aligned with expert knowledge? To address this gap, we present FIX (Features Interpretable to eXperts), a benchmark for measuring how well a collection of features aligns with expert knowledge. In collaboration with domain experts, we propose FIXScore, a unified expert alignment measure applicable to diverse real-world settings across cosmology, psychology, and medicine domains in vision, language, and time series data modalities. With FIXScore, we find that popular feature-based explanation methods have poor alignment with expert-specified knowledge, highlighting the need for new methods that can better identify features interpretable to experts.
evaluation_method: FIXScore — an expert-alignment scoring metric (expert annotations / agreement-based scoring); reported as a composite expert-alignment score
reputation: A recent benchmark (FIXScore) aimed at expert alignment across multiple domains; currently of interest to researchers in interpretability but not yet widely adopted.
notes: Requires domain expert annotations and domain-specific ground truth; multimodal and cross-domain so scores may not be comparable across tasks; non-LLM (feature/interpretability) benchmark and potentially limited in scale per domain.
